meta.title: Pyreon docs
meta.description: Guides, API reference and live examples for Pyreon: one TypeScript codebase for the web, iOS and Android.

banner.label: experimental
banner.text: iOS and Android are experimental. The capability matrix shows exactly what is proven on a real simulator and emulator today.
banner.source: docs/src/content/docs/multiplatform.md (status line and "Production capability matrix (weighted, rung-labeled)"); stability-and-direction.md

hero.title: Build the website. Get the apps.
hero.lede: Pyreon is a full-stack TypeScript framework with 40 products in the box. Pick where you are starting, and the docs take it from there.

startHere.title: I'm building a website
startHere.text: SSR, SSG, ISR or SPA per route, with forms, data and the store already wired.

startHere.title: I want the phone apps too
startHere.text: One `src/App.tsx` compiled to SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose, next to the website. Experimental.

startHere.title: I'm coming from React
startHere.text: Swap `react` imports for the compat layer, keep shipping, and port screens to signals when it pays.

alt.label: or start fresh with compat wired in

startHere.title: I just need one product
startHere.text: Forms, charts, i18n, validation: each one installs on its own, without the rest of the stack.

tiles.title: Products people start with
tiles.text: Each card carries one number from the benchmark record, with the conditions it was measured under.

proof.label: faster server rendering than React 19 at 1,000 rows (compiled SSR, 109.9 vs 714.4 µs)
proof.condition: one run, overnight pass, M3 Max, synthetic, author-run

proof.label: faster mount than React Hook Form (12 fields, 210 vs 640 µs); fastest of 7 libraries on all 4 timed ops
proof.condition: one run, overnight pass, real Chromium

proof.label: cells won against zod, valibot and arktype on a multi-schema workload
faster than ECharts 6 mounting a 100,000-point line chart (4.36 vs 37.95 ms)
proof.condition: one run, final pass, real Chromium

proof.label: operations won against React Flow 12 (500 nodes): mount, drag, select, add, pan and zoom, unmount
proof.condition: one run, real Chromium, synthetic, author-run
proof.source: 00-brief/BENCHMARKS-2026-11-05.md §2 flow vs React Flow 12: wins all six ops, 1.17–210×, one run. Headline uses 6/6, not 210×: the record says the drag/pan ratios are mostly React Flow re-rendering node wrappers

proof.label: faster effect propagation than Preact Signals

whyFast.title: Why it's fast
whyFast.text: Components run once. The compiler binds each signal to the exact DOM node that reads it, so a click updates one text node: no virtual DOM to diff, nothing to memoise, no dependency arrays.

live.note: Mounted live with `<Example>`: the function runs once, and the text node updates on every click.

link.label: Components run once, step by step

whyFast.source: Compiled with transformJSX (packages/core/compiler) on e314cc619; output trimmed of the import line and formatting only.

items.label: faster than React 19 creating 10,000 rows (72.6 vs 192.0 ms)
items.condition: real Chromium, final pass run 1 table

items.label: for the same keyed-table app, gzip; React ships 69.6 KB (and Solid 7.5 KB, which we print too)
retained heap after the row suite, tied lightest framework with Preact (3.09 MB)
faster server rendering than React 19 at 1,000 rows (compiled SSR, 109.9 vs 714.4 µs)
items.condition: one run, overnight pass, M3 Max, synthetic, author-run

proofStrip.footer: Synthetic, author-run, Apple M3 Max, record of 5 Nov 2026. Every loss is on the same page, and so are the claims this record withdrew.

whatsNew.title: What's new on main
whatsNew.text: Merged since the last release and shipping in the next one. Until it publishes, `npm create @pyreon/zero@latest` installs the current release without these.

items.title: `effect()` runs on iOS and Android
items.text: Runs when the view appears and again when a signal it reads changes, cleanup included. Before, it was dropped with a warning.

items.title: More plain TypeScript compiles natively
items.text: Timers, `Date`, `enum`s, module-scope signals, `throw` / `try` / `catch`, `JSON.parse` and a schema's `.parse()` now lower to Swift and Kotlin.

items.title: `<Select>` and date and time fields
items.text: One choice with each platform's own picker, and `<Field kind="date" | "time" | "datetime">` with `min` / `max` on web, iOS and Android.

items.title: Eight more hooks lower to iOS and Android
`queryOptions()`: declare a query once
items.text: Reuse it in hooks and in the client; the key carries the data type, so `getQueryData(opts.queryKey)` is typed without a generic.

items.title: `mode: 'auto'` prerenders the routes it infers as SSG
items.text: Even in a build that also has SSR routes. One resolver now answers "what mode does this page get" everywhere. `auto` stays experimental.

items.title: One copy of each head tag after hydration
items.text: Server-rendered pages no longer end up with two of every `<meta>`, `<link>` and JSON-LD tag. Also: `createUniqueId()` ids now match between server and client.

items.title: `@pyreon/validate/mini`
items.text: Ships without the runtime JIT: a 4-field object schema is 5.2 KB gzip through `mini` vs 13.8 KB through the main entry (author-measured). `enableJit()` brings the JIT back.

items.title: Scheduled entries
items.text: `publishDate` plus `unpublished: 'omit'` keeps future-dated posts out of a production build; they appear with the first build on or after their date. It is how pyreon.dev/blog publishes.

items.title: Heads-up: `subscribe` changed shape
items.text: The state is now `mutation.state`, built on first read; the second `state` argument is gone. Update `subscribe((mutation, state) => …)` callbacks when you upgrade.

whatsNew.footer: Plus security hardening in Zero, MCP, Lathe, the native WebView and the serialisers, and a batch of fixes found by new browser gates on the example apps.
